question: Can an in-house sorted-vector flat_map replace std::map for Detent's four public model tables with equal correctness, lower memory and acceptable CPU?
platform: macOS arm64, Apple clang 17, Release (-O3 -DNDEBUG), 100,000 knobs, three alternating-start arms, five rounds per workload, medians

design.storage: std::vector<std::pair<Key,T>> sorted unique; value_type non-const key; static_assert nothrow move
design.bulk: flat_map_builder appends, tracks strict ascent, one index sort for unsorted input; first duplicate in input order via min over groups of the second occurrence
design.merge: flat_map_merge linear pass used by apply_patch, diff_snapshots, compose_patches, merge_over_defaults
design.drains: four authority disposal drains erase std::prev(end()) instead of begin()

correctness.ctest: 210/210 pass (build-flat, after fixing my own precedence test); includes test_model_alloc_failure, new test_flat_map and test_duplicate_precedence
correctness.ctest_first_run: two failures: test_duplicate_precedence (test bug: parse_defaults rejects "version"; fixed) and test_local_paged_snapshot_plan (StoragePressure abort, flaky: 1 failure in 8 runs on the flat arm and 1 in 6 on the std::map arm, passes on rerun)
correctness.precedence_tests_on_std_map_arm: test_duplicate_precedence compiled against the std::map arm (build-adopt libdetent) also passes: the new tests encode the old behavior
correctness.canonical_bytes: test_snapshot_canonical: snapshot.json and snapshot.shm cmp-identical to .scratch/canon-adopt
correctness.lifecycle_digests: --knobs 2000 and --knobs 2000 --long --random digests equal the std::map arm; all four 100k configs digests equal across std_map, flat, btree

quadratic_guard_seconds.note: two runs per arm, medians of two shown for flat/adopt first run; second run within 15%; duplicate message identical

correctness.iterator_holders: state.cc 306/445/1372, change_history.cc 95, export_encoder.cc 38, read_reply.cc 126 hold iterators only into const definitions (command mutations or shared_ptr<const KnobDef> records) that are not mutated meanwhile; none reported
correctness.examples: examples/ build in build-flat (examples/publish_snapshot.cc keeps a BoolDef& from as_bool only until its next use, before any further insert)
correctness.bindings: not built (DETENT_BUILD_PYTHON/RUST off); sources do not touch the four tables (only cli_overrides vectors)

btree_recorded_retained_requested_bytes_.note: different workload than lifecycle_bench; compare ratios within lifecycle_bench rows

commands.pairs: quiet exclusive flat-pairs 75 'flat vs std::map model pairs' -- python3 flat-wt/.scratch/flat_pair.py OUT (arms std_map=build-adopt, flat=build-flat, btree=build-base; start arm rotated per pair)

limits: macOS arm64 only; GCC 11/libstdc++ Linux not built, so Linux LeakSanitizer run of test_model_alloc_failure not taken
ASan hangs at startup on this host (even an empty program), so only UBSan ran on test_flat_map

lifecycle_bench cleanup stage in the flat arm erases the LAST override (the authority drain shape); std_map and btree arms were built from the older bench that erases begin(); flat also records an erase-begin variant (cleanup_begin_turn_ns)
prune_half_positional is the positional-erase pathology (not a Detent production operation)
decoder (state.cc 142/656) grows overrides by doubling; no reserve at count
diff_snapshots shrink_to_fit after a single pass costs extra requested bytes (transient)
fleet corpus and 1.3M capacity tier not measured
